name: APA Jamii Plus – Family Cover (KES 500,000)
note:
Jamii Plus Health Cover – quotation terms

Premiums. Annual premiums in Kenya Shillings from the APA Jamii Plus rate card (rates as at May 2026). Inpatient premiums depend on each member's current age and the family limit chosen; the inpatient limit is shared by the family. Outpatient, dental and optical cover are priced per person, and the same benefits and limits apply to all members of the policy. Maternity is priced per family. Dental and optical can only be bought together with outpatient cover. Premiums exclude taxes: Training Levy (0.2%) and Policyholders' Compensation Fund levy (0.25%) are added, plus KES 40 stamp duty per policy.

Outpatient benefits by limit. Also covered at every level: prescription drugs (up to 30 days), X-ray, MRI, CT scan and other diagnostic tests, prescribed physiotherapy, chiropractors and osteopaths on GP referral, pre-existing and chronic conditions including HIV/AIDS (after 12 months), congenital and prematurity conditions (after 12 months), newly diagnosed chronic conditions (after 3 months), prenatal and postnatal consultations with up to 2 obstetric scans (after 10 months, where maternity is bought), HPV and flu vaccination, yellow fever and polio travel vaccines, and prescribed nutritional supplements.

Outpatient benefit50,00075,000100,000150,000200,000
GP consultation limit per visit2,0002,5003,0003,0003,000
Specialist fees (on GP referral)3,0003,0003,500Up to 4,000Up to 4,000
Family planning and related complications (selected facilities)5,0007,50010,00010,00010,000
Prescribed emollients and pharmaceutical creams (Oilatum, Epimax, Epimol, Oatveen Eczema)5,0007,50010,00010,00010,000
Occupational and speech therapy, delayed milestones (after 12 months)15,00015,00020,00025,00025,000
KEPI and baby-friendly vaccines (children up to 18 months)15,00015,00020,00025,00025,000
General health check-up (age 21 and above)5,0007,50010,00015,00020,000
External appliances, hearing aids and hearing tests15,00015,00020,00025,00025,000

Outpatient co-payments. KES 1,000 at the Aga Khan Group of Hospitals (Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu) and The Nairobi Hospital. KES 500 at Mater Hospital, M.P. Shah Hospital, AAR Healthcare & Hospital, Gertrude's Children's, Premier Hospital, The Mombasa Hospital, Diani Beach Hospital, Pandya Memorial Hospital, Jocham Hospital, Palm Beach Hospital, Eldoret Hospital, Oasis Doctors Plaza, Oasis Healthcare Group and Mediheal Group of Hospitals (including satellite clinics). No co-payment at all other providers.

Waiting periods.

  • Accidents: none. Acute illness: 30 days. Newly diagnosed chronic conditions: 3 months.
  • Pre-existing and chronic illnesses, palliative care and congenital conditions: 12 months.
  • Surgery not related to a pre-existing or chronic illness: 90 days. Procedures ending in "-tomy" (e.g. fibroid removal, hernia repair, adenoidectomy, tonsillectomy, gynaecological surgery, haemorrhoids): 12 months.
  • Maternity and related conditions: 10 months. Organ transplant: 2 years.

Eligibility.

  • Ages: from day 1 (full-term baby at 38 weeks) up to 80 years. Spouses and children older than 3 months who are not added at the start of cover go on a separate policy, with waiting periods.
  • Members joining from age 60 must have a medical examination at an APA-approved provider, at their own cost.
  • Full disclosure of all material facts is required; non-disclosure leads to non-payment of claims and cancellation without refund. Undeclared pre-existing conditions stay excluded for the life of the policy.
  • Either party may cancel with 14 days' notice. No refund for members deleted after 6 months of cover or where claims have been made.

Using the cover.

  • Inpatient bills are paid net of SHIF benefits. Area of cover: East Africa, plus up to 6 weeks of emergency treatment a year on reimbursement when travelling outside Kenya (notify APA before travelling).
  • Outpatient cover is accessed with a biometric card at the APA panel of providers. Treatment outside the panel is reimbursed at up to 85% of APA rates; claims older than 90 days are not payable.
  • Planned admissions must be reported to APA at least 48 hours before admission and pre-authorised. In an emergency, the hospital notifies APA within 24 hours.
  • Renewal is subject to claims experience and underwriting. Benefit upgrades are accepted from the third year of cover, with waiting periods on new benefits. A break in cover of more than 30 days restarts waiting periods.

Main exclusions. Expenses recoverable from other insurance (e.g. SHIF, WIBA, GPA); cosmetic or plastic surgery unless after an accident; beauty treatment; senility; allergy tests; infertility treatment (other than under maternity cover); participation in riots, strikes or civil commotion; injuries from drunkenness, intentional self-injury or attempted suicide; naval, military or air-force operations; war and nuclear contamination; personal care items not covered under outpatient; sexually transmitted diseases; pain management; weight-management treatment; experimental, herbal or acupuncture treatment; hearing aids and tests in the first 12 months; eye glasses and dental treatment unless optical or dental cover is bought or under inpatient benefits; and any benefit not bought.

Payment. Pay APA Insurance Limited directly: NCBA Bank Kenya, account 6447560039 (Westlands branch), or M-Pesa Paybill 511600 (account: principal member's name for new business, policy number for renewals). Always get an official APA receipt. Cover starts once APA has received the full premium.

This quotation is valid for 30 days and is subject to APA's underwriting and acceptance. Benefits are a summary; the APA policy document prevails.
